decisions.reason: The report grounds itself in package.json and the README, states alpha.1 was never published while alpha.2 was, and proposes per-package verification (npm view ... versions) while explicitly warning against inferring internal package availability from a dist-tag or the root package, matching the brief-supplied registry fact.

It correctly explains the caret range expansion (>=0.1.2-alpha.1 <0.2.0-0), that install silently succeeds by resolving to the published 0.1.2-alpha.2, the resulting declaration/type-baseline drift, and the lack of compatibility guarantees across alpha prereleases. It does not claim all alphas are missing or that the caret guarantees alpha.1.

Two coherent plans are given: (A) check out an exact upstream alpha.1 source ref, build/pack, and pin the local tarball via overrides with a registry range for later; (B) exactly pin the published 0.1.2-alpha.2 while explicitly acknowledging this never validates alpha.1. Tradeoffs are stated for each, exceeding the one-plan minimum.

The plan includes a committed lockfile with frozen install (npm ci / pnpm ci), a single consistent package manager (explicitly forbidding mixing), a tsc --noEmit typecheck gate, and an exit path for path A (delete the overrides once an official release exists and return to registry resolution). Registry facts are framed as to-be-verified rather than asserted, satisfying honest handling of unverified details.
